chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: The pact with Trumbauer to share credit; Three Blind Mice
summary: Virginia says Chauncey and Frankie shared everything; Morehouse wrote Three Blind Mice, his best-known song, but shared credit under their pact.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: You see, Chauncey and Frankie made a pact between themselves. They were very close. They made a pact that no matter what one had, they would share.
They would share whatever they had between themselves.
It had been said that Chauncey Morehouse did not write, did not necessarily write ......
But they were two young fellows.
Chauncey, darling, you told me that you wrote most of Three Blind Mice.
You wrote Three Blind Mice together.
That was your best known song.
(HUMS AND BEATS OUT THREE BLIND MICE)
That was your best known song. Okay. Did Frankie Trumbauer write any of that?
You wrote that. But you shared credit with him because you had this pact.
